description:
FILED s451y (Opus, round 10 agent Y) from the #610 probes.  PRE-EXISTING on
main 718db6b, and it covers the WHOLE list-assignment family -- not just the
#610 shape, which is why it is a task and not part of that fix.

WHAT PERL DOES: a list assignment used as a VALUE yields
  * in SCALAR context: the number of elements the RHS produced   (PCL: right)
  * in LIST   context: the LHS, as lvalues, AFTER the assignment (PCL: WRONG --
    it returns the scalar-context count, as a one-element list)

REPRO (perl vs ./runpcl), all three measured on 718db6b:
    sub v3 { my ($a, undef) = (10,20,30) }
    my $s = v3(); my @l = v3();
    print "[$s][@l]\n";
        perl: [3][10 20]
        PCL:  [3][3]

    sub v2 { my (undef, undef) = (10,20,30) }      # needs #610 to transpile
        perl: [3][10 20]
        PCL:  [3][3]

    my @l = ((undef) = (10,20,30));                # a plain expression, no `my`
        perl: [10]
        PCL:  []

    my @l = (() = (10,20,30));                     # the countof idiom
        perl: []
        PCL:  []      <-- this one AGREES

So the empty LHS `()` is right and every non-empty LHS is wrong; the `undef`
placeholder counts as an LHS element that takes a value (perl returns the 10).

WHY IT MATTERS: the shape is the tail statement of a sub -- `sub f { my ($a,
$b) = @_ }` called in list context -- which is a common accidental spelling,
and the countof idiom `my $n = () = f()` is the one PCL gets right, so the
divergence is invisible until someone uses the list form.

WHERE TO LOOK: `Pl::ExprToCL`'s `=` dispatch for the list forms (p-list-= /
p-array-= / p-hash-=) and the runtime `p-list-=` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp -- the
return value, not the assignment.  The context is already known at the node
(the scalar answer is right), so the list answer is the missing arm.

BAR: the four rows above vs perl in both contexts, plus the container LHS
(`my @a = (1,2,3)` used as a value -- perl returns the ARRAY's elements) and
the hash LHS; corpus-diff + emission-ab (a return-value emission change);
guard rows beside the #610 family in Pl/t/aassign-01.t.
subject: a list assignment used as a VALUE in LIST context returns the scalar COUNT, where perl returns the LHS lvalues: `sub f { my ($a,undef) = (10,20,30) }` gives (3) not (10,20)
